data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 never addresses the problem's required second half: it explains why a panel might be more reliable, but provides no evidence-within-a-single-evaluation criterion to distinguish genuine reliability gain from checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. Its variance-reduction framing is equally consistent with members blindly copying checklist outputs (pure compliance) and with genuine independent convergence; both produce low variance around the correct answer, so the covering principle it offers does not separate the two phenomena the problem asks it to separate.
